reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is a practical walkthrough for contacting eBay support through the eBay help page while logged in. It shows customer-service navigation, issue selection, a phone number, and an issue-specific passcode as part of that support process, while discussing access problems and inaccurate wait-time messaging rather than soliciting money, credentials, or participation in a financial scheme.

citations.quote: be logged into your account and go on that page ebay.com slash help slash. Home.
now you need to select your problem.
they will give you a phone number
Waiting time wait time is two minutes that's absolutely not true

opening.argument: The video links a concrete viewer action to obtaining help with an eBay account or transaction: viewers are told to select a problem, call the displayed number, and provide a one-time passcode. That is a low-friction verification flow presented as the route to resolving selling, payment, or refund issues. The video does not establish who controls the number or what happens after the code is provided, so the apparent support benefit is being used to induce contact and disclosure of an account-related code.

citations.quote: now you need to select your problem.
they will give you a phone number

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a walkthrough does not resolve the central risk. The cited navigation only shows that a page displays a call option; it does not prove that the displayed number is trustworthy or that providing the one-time code is safe. The video itself emphasizes contacting the number and supplying the code, while the claimed two-minute estimate is expressly challenged as inaccurate.

citations.quote: Waiting time wait time is two minutes that's absolutely not true

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument treats ordinary support verification as an asset-acquisition scheme without showing any reward, payment, account transfer, or financial return. The page is presented as eBay Customer Service and the video directs viewers to the official help page, where issue selection leads to a contact option. A one-time passcode and a phone number establish a support workflow, not a promise of acquiring an asset.

citations.quote: go on that page ebay.com slash help slash. Home

opening.argument: Several genuine warning signs appear together: a branded customer-service page presents a phone number and requests a one-time passcode, while the narration says callers may need to try repeatedly because the lines are overwhelmed. The viewer is therefore encouraged to keep contacting a purported support channel despite uncertainty about its availability and despite an identification code being requested. That combination can facilitate low-barrier access to account-related benefits or assets, even though the video supplies no independent proof that the contact route is legitimate.

citations.quote: Try many times in a day many times in a week

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense highlights the page's appearance and issue categories, but those features are precisely what can make a contact route persuasive. It does not answer why an identification code must be disclosed to the caller, nor does it establish that the displayed contact details are authentic. The narration's claim that lines are overwhelmed adds pressure to persist rather than independent reassurance.

citations.quote: you really need to be very persistent and very patient

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not the red flags associated with an asset-acquisition scam. There is no reward, investment return, purchase, deposit, or withdrawal promise. The displayed page offers issue-specific assistance for selling fees and other ordinary eBay problems, and the narration warns viewers that access may be difficult rather than promising an easy benefit.

citations.quote: i didn't get paid for an item. I sold or something like this

opening.argument: Although framed as an educational explanation, the video actively promotes a particular contact pathway: viewers are directed to the help page, told to choose a problem, shown a phone number, and instructed to use an issue-specific identifier. The repeated focus on how to reach the service turns the tutorial into a call-to-action for contacting that channel. Because the video cannot independently establish what the caller receives after completing that flow, its practical effect is to steer viewers toward a potentially unsafe account-verification interaction.

citations.quote: Here's how to Call Ebay for any help
be logged into your account and go on that page ebay.com slash help slash. Home.
so you really need to be very persistent and very patient

rebuttal.rebuttal: The word 'help' in the description does not prove the pathway is safe or merely educational. The important behavior being promoted is not just browsing: it is calling a displayed number and entering a one-time code. The defense also leaves unaddressed that the video says the stated wait time is not true and that callers may repeatedly encounter an inability to answer.

citations.quote: you call them you. Get a message saying we are upgrading our system we cannot answer in this moment
Waiting time wait time is two minutes that's absolutely not true

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a support procedure is not promotion of a scam category. The video does not solicit money, a purchase, a deposit, or a promised reward; it explains how to navigate a page and openly criticizes the service's availability. The call option and issue-specific identifier are shown as parts of troubleshooting, not as a route to acquiring an asset.

citations.quote: So depending on your problem you need an ID.
they are really hard to reach
